answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed lighthouse keeper's post on a real coast: the keeper tends one lamp, logs every voyage that passes its beam in a public trellis of light records, and must repeat a whispered one-time code from the tower radio within minutes when paged, a call one operator cannot answer from two towers at once. A license fee paid in outside money doubles for each further post on the same funding trail, so every extra fake identity costs another real lighthouse, another keeper on night watch, and twice the previous fee.
